problem: For integers r>=2, k>=1, a_1..a_k>=1, b>=1 let P(q) = [a_1]_q...[a_k]_q * [b]_{q^r}, where [n]_q = 1+q+...+q^{n-1} and [b]_{q^r} = 1+q^r+...+q^{r(b-1)}. P is (weakly) unimodal if its coefficients satisfy c_0<=...<=c_m>=...>=c_N for some m. U = {b : P unimodal}, F = sum floor(a_i/r), D = sum(a_i-1). Question: exactly which parameters make P unimodal? (Source: arXiv:2605.12822, Conjecture 5.4.)

claims.statement: THEOREM: Conjecture S2 holds for r=4, 5, 6, for every k and all part sizes: if r divides no a_i then U = [1,B*] or [1,B*]\{B*-1}. Computer-assisted: Lemma 1 (L' at n*(C) for every pair => S2), V bounds, operator lemmas, covering criterion; r=4: exhaustive exact-tail check k'<=15, analytic certificate 12<=k<=140, hand proof k>=141; r=5: own residue certificate + R2E2 Theorem R for k<=23 (fit-box-excluded classes covered analytically with V<=5), analytic 24<=k<=140, hand proof k>=141; r=6: residue certificate + Theorem R for k<=53 (excluded classes via V<=11), analytic 54<=k<=140, hand proof k>=141. REFEREE NOTES: (a) check that the 'fit-box-excluded' residue classes that the explorer skipped in its residue certificate (790 for r=5, 4,893 + 35,397 for r=6) are genuinely covered by the analytic argument, i.e. that the case split leaves NO instance uncovered (you may compute anything, there is no box for you); (b) a separate round-3 explorer showed that the residue certificate condition O_rho of Theorem R is FALSE for some rho with many parts equal to 1 (e.g. r=57) - check that the r=5 (k<=23) and r=6 (k<=53) uses of Theorem R only rely on certificates actually verified for those rho; (c) check the k>=141 hand proofs line by line. Context: earlier refereed results may be cited: round-2 synthesis /tmp/claude-0/qu/synth/r2/proof.txt (class-pair Thms 3.1, 4.2), round-2 proofs under /tmp/claude-0/qu/explore2/R2E*/ (T9-T15), round-1 synthesis /tmp/claude-0/qu/synth/r1/proof.txt; check that every cited result is used exactly as stated there.

T15 holds for all r>=4 and all nm: r divides no a_i, exactly three a_i of middle residue (in [2,r-2]), all others residue 1 or r-1 => U = [1,B*], B* = T6 - 2*[tau_s<=-2 and s>=2mu] (tau = (1-q)prod[rho_i]_q mod q^r-1, mu = largest j in [1,r-1] with tau_j>0, T6 = 1+floor((D+1-2mu)/r), s = (D+1) mod r). Removes the previous restriction r<=30, nm<=37.
